A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same LinuxFLBench benchmark and LinuxFL+ framework despite the changed title and formatting. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original fault-localization experiments on 250 LinuxFLBench bugs, including baseline comparisons, enhancement results, component ablations, and statistical analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds model comparisons, retrieval and reranking experiments, and analyses of benchmark characteristics and failure conditions.

M1.justification: The proposed directory-aware expansion, direct and mail-augmented hypotheses, reciprocal-rank merging, and LLM reranking remain unchanged. Additional backbone evaluations and experimental component combinations do not establish a revision to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: The same 250 LinuxFLBench bugs and file-level and method-level localization tasks are retained. New symptom/difficulty partitions and the 50-task study use retained data. SWE-bench Lite receives additional characterization within the existing SWE-bench comparison; KBENCHSYZ remains related-work material.

E2.justification: The main three-agent and four-IR comparator set is unchanged. Appendix E adds direct BM25 retrieval as a mail-retrieval comparator and BM25 rerankers using file paths or contents in Table 13. Direct LLM Hypothesis is the retained standalone strategy under a clearer label.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-32B enhancement evaluations and a random 50-task Agentless study covering Qwen3 sizes, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, substantially broadening model configurations and evaluation design. It also introduces symptom/difficulty stratification and new component controls. The combined Direct Hypothesis experiments merge agent predictions with hypotheses and rerank them; these differ from v1's standalone hypothesis evaluations.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: benchmark-complexity analyses in Appendix A.3, symptom and localization-cue analyses in Sections 4.2 and 5.3.3, standalone-versus-combined hypothesis experiments, mail-retrieval recall and recovered/lost-file analysis, and BM25 reranking controls in Appendix E. The original qualitative failure cases and component analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix G/Table 7 and v2 Appendix H/Table 12 report the same means, standard deviations, paired t-tests, confidence intervals, and 1,000-resample statement. V2 adds no repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting procedure for its new experiments.

E6.justification: The original GPT-4o baseline, enhancement, method-level, and cost results remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear for model variants, difficulty groups, benchmark characteristics, retrieval, and reranking. V1's standalone Direct Hypothesis Recall@1 of 0.316 is retained separately; v2 adds agent-combined values of 0.440, 0.444, and 0.412 under different procedures. The new 50-task GPT-5 comparison reports MRR of 0.569 before enhancement and 0.668 afterward.

T1.justification: The fault-localization task definition and reciprocal-rank aggregation formula are mathematically unchanged, although v2 places them inline instead of in numbered displays. Neither version adds or removes substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark contribution, the finding that existing agents struggle with kernel localization, and the LinuxFL+ enhancement claim. The headline 41.6% baseline accuracy and 7.2–11.2 percentage-point improvements remain unchanged; the new title does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: V2 extends the existing mechanism explanations by linking ambiguous symptoms to potential-cause expansion, weak localization cues to directory expansion, and reranking advantages to semantic rather than lexical matching. It also discusses applicability across stronger and smaller models and updates the different-LLM limitation while acknowledging that exploration remains limited.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the December 31, 2024 bug-collection cutoff, ctags and trajectory checks for the previously described C/C++ adaptation, and annotators' programming experience. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the existing dataset or adaptation changed. Prompt templates and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Qwen3 technical report for the new backbone evaluations. The existing fault-localization and benchmark literature is retained, with the KBENCHSYZ positioning discussion condensed. Most reference changes concern citation style or bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and corresponding-author designation, tightens several introductory, related-work, and method passages, places limitations after the conclusion, and adds headings for new analyses. The overall narrative and most existing explanations remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. All nine figure images are retained unchanged. V1's combined performance/cost table becomes v2 Tables 5–6, the ablation table is reorganized, and several new analysis tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through clearer standalone-versus-combined hypothesis evaluation, targeted BM25 controls, failure analyses, and tests beyond GPT-4o. These partially address v1's component-attribution and model-coverage limitations. The net gain is limited by the 50-task scope of most additional backbone tests and some overstated interpretation: Table 8 improves Hard-case MRR, but the absolute Easy/Hard gap increases from 0.331 to 0.354 rather than narrowing.
